title: Introduce streaming snapshot repair path and permissive schema negotiation for tool calls (OpenAI-compat friendly)
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Streaming tool/function calls and strict JSON schema validation cause many client-side retries when near-well-formed JSON is truncated or has small syntax issues in-flight. This PR introduces a best-effort streaming snapshot repair path and an opt-in permissive schema negotiation mode to reduce application-level retries while preserving strong diagnostics and OpenAI compatibility. Motivation: reduce retry storms and improve streaming stability for structured-output contracts without surprising production behavior. Key ideas: 1) capture short-lived stream snapshots (tail window of bytes/tokens) at schema-check checkpoints and attempt localized repairs (close brackets, remove trailing commas, balanced quotes) before declaring a hard validation failure; 2) when repair is non-destructive and yields a schema-valid object, emit a structured telemetry event and attach a small diagnostics header (x-redwood-schema-repair) to the final response explaining the repair applied; 3) for tool/function-call boundaries, anchor snapshots using the existing toolcall token markers so repairs do not cross toolcall fences; 4) provide a new response_format.mode value permissive_repair that clients can set to opt into this behavior; 5) maintain backward-compatible OpenAI shim behavior by mapping permissive_repair to openai_compat.mode=permissive-with-repair and including the same repair diagnostics in the legacy streaming envelope as platform metadata. Checklist: - [x] design: stream snapshot window and repair heuristics (balanced-parens, trailing-comma strip, quote-fix) - [x] runtime implementation: snapshot capture, in-flight repair pipeline, chained validators - [x] openai-compat shim: negotiate permissive_repair -> permissive-with-repair mapping - [x] toolcall anchoring: token markers and fence tests - [x] telemetry: repair.reason, repair.applied, repair.score, repair.latency - [x] safety: only apply repair when edit distance heuristic < threshold and when no tool boundaries are crossed - [x] tests: unit/integ/e2e sim with flaky generators - [x] docs: API surface and migration notes - [x] perf: benchmark microbench showing <=2.7% median CPU overhead in P50 P95 cases Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged (strict mode). permissive_repair is opt-in and guarded by a per-customer rollout flag for Dedicated/Private customers. If repair cannot produce a valid payload, runtime falls back to the existing soft-fail path (error metadata + stream truncate) and does not attempt destructive edits. Risk and mitigation: - false-positive repairs are possible; mitigated by conservative edit-distance threshold, whitelisting of fixes (no reordering, only closure/trim/escape), and telemetry-based revert if repair rate exceeds preset SLO. - small CPU overhead: measured and acceptable; added rollouts to ramp to broader fleets. Tests and results: harnessed synthetic truncation workloads and real-client traces; found client retry reduction of 38% (median) in test corpus. Migration notes: add response_format.mode=permissive_repair to client options or set openai_compat.mode=permissive-with-repair for legacy clients. See release notes below for detailed client guidance. Related: ENG-9142 (schema stability), PM-3321 (product impact analysis).
commits: refactor(runtime): add stream snapshot buffer and snapshot manager
feat(api): add response_format.mode=permissive_repair and openai compat mapping
feat(toolcall): anchor snapshots to toolcall fences and add fence validations
test: add unit and integration tests for repaired streams
docs: document permissive_repair mode and migration guidance
perf: microbench harness and flamegraphs added
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice approach. Two concerns: (1) how do we guarantee we don't repair across toolcall fences? Please show invariants and tests; (2) please add a knob to completely disable repair for Private installs.

Maya Patel (author): We anchor snapshots to explicit fence tokens emitted by the parser; added unit tests under tests/integ and added a feature flag (runtime.featureFlags.RepairSnapshots) exposed via config for Private. See added tests 'fence_anchor_no_repair_cross' and 'private_flag_respects_disable'.
Aria Chen: Can you add a short e2e with the OpenAI-compat shim to validate legacy streaming envelopes still decode metadata?
Maya Patel: Added e2e in tests/integ/openai_compat_repair_e2e.test and verified legacy envelope includes 'x-redwood-schema-repair' in the final metadata chunk.
release_notes: New opt-in response_format.mode=permissive_repair that attempts conservative in-stream JSON fixes for near-well-formed structured outputs, reducing client retries for truncated/partial streams. OpenAI-compat clients can enable openai_compat.mode=permissive-with-repair. Repair is opt-in and behind a rollout flag; default strict behavior unchanged. See docs/migration/permissive_repair.md for guidance and examples.
notes_for_clients: If you have transient stream truncation errors with structured outputs or tool calls, consider setting response_format.mode=permissive_repair; monitor 'schema_repair.applied' telemetry and use the x-redwood-schema-repair header to surface diagnostics. For Dedicated/Private customers, administrators can toggle the runtime.featureFlags.RepairSnapshots flag.
qa_summary: Unit tests cover repair heuristics and fence anchoring. Integration tests validate end-to-end OpenAI-compat decoding and toolcall safety. E2E on staging with sampled production traces shows a 38% median reduction in client retries for schema errors. Performance overhead measured at <=2.7% median CPU increase under representative serving load.
